parts.note: Both 33.0 degrees. Checked: sin OAC = 5 sin 1.2 / 8.5667 = 0.5440, OAC = 32.96; acute since opposite the shortest side, so no sine-rule ambiguity.

key_verdict: Key and blind examiner agree on every part; all four values re-derived and confirmed.
fixes: Part (b) is still a routine sine-rule read-off that nothing later uses. Make it the non-routine step and load-bearing: replace it with 'Calculate angle ACB. Give your answer in degrees. [2]' (or angle OCA). The candidate must then find OAC by the sine rule AND convert 1.2 rad to 68.75 degrees AND use the exterior angle: ACB = 68.75 + 32.96 = 101.7 degrees (OCA = 78.3 degrees). The radian-to-degree mix is exactly the slip a real 4052 question tests; marks stay at 9.
Drop 'drawn to scale' from the figure spec; SEAB figures carry no scale statement and the printed figure should not imply one.
Stem wording to the SEAB pattern: 'The diagram shows a sector OAB of a circle, centre O, radius 9 cm.' and 'The shaded region is bounded by AC, CB and the arc AB.'
why: The shape (sector minus a triangle on a radius, cosine rule in radians, perimeter then area) is a genuine 4052 P2 shape with clean numbers, a consistent figure and correct part labels and mark splits, and it re-skins none of the exemplars; it stops short of 5 because the added part (b) is a standalone routine step that the rest of the question never needs, so the repair has not yet supplied the non-routine step the first moderator asked for.
